title: Stalk of a higher direct image along a spectral map as cohomology on the set of specialisations
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter cohomology.tex (Cohomology of Sheaves)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file cohomology.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
difficulty_reason: For a spectral map of spectral spaces f: X to Y, a point y, the set E of points specializing to y and an abelian sheaf F on X, the lemma identifies the stalk at y of the p-th higher direct image with the cohomology of F on the inverse image of E (statement lines 3893-3899). The proof observes that E is the intersection of the quasi-compact open neighbourhoods of y, so its inverse image is the filtered intersection of the inverse images, which are spectral spaces because f is spectral; hence the inverse image of E is a spectral space and its cohomology is the colimit of the cohomologies of the inverse images of the neighbourhoods, by the colimit lemma for spectral spaces (proof lines 3901-3911). The other side of the identity is exactly that colimit, since stalks of higher direct images are computed as colimits over the quasi-compact open neighbourhoods (proof lines 3912-3913). The claim is H2: the identification of the two colimits is the content, with the spectrality of the pieces as the input that makes the colimit lemma applicable.
